issue_request: FHIR-19300 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 OO change request asking FHIR-core Task to provide an example value set for Task.code, with useful common activity codes such as please fulfill, please suspend, and please cancel.
initial_application: The issue was applied in source history by 7476beb8fa (GF#19300), before the Jira GH#de65b7ad merge pointer. That commit added source/task/codesystem-task-code.xml and source/task/valueset-task-code.xml, and changed the then-current Task spreadsheet binding from unbound to an example binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/task-code.
additional_context: Task is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/task is current build scope. Current source still defines the Task Codes value set and code system, including common activity codes such as fulfill, suspend, abort/cancel-like actions, change, replace, resume, approve, instantiate, and data-request. Later FHIR-37001 intentionally changed Task.code binding strength from example to extensible while retaining the same value set.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The requested value set exists in current build-scope source and remains wired to Task.code; the non-example binding strength is a later accepted decision rather than an incomplete application of FHIR-19300.
